mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, let’s bring these ideas together. At the heart of it all is a simple truth: government should serve the people—never rule over them from some distant throne. Real leadership? It’s something you earn with your character and your actions, not something you’re handed at birth. And the right to govern ourselves isn’t just a privilege—it’s a responsibility, and it’s where our dignity comes from. When things feel uncertain or change is on the horizon, unity and courage are what see us through. The fight for justice and freedom? It never really ends. It’s a challenge passed down from one generation to the next, always asking for our effort and our heart. The story of “Common Sense” isn’t just a snapshot from history. It’s a reminder—a call to ask, “Why not something better?” What those American colonists started still echoes today, because the power to shape the world isn’t locked away with rulers or tied up in old traditions. It’s right here, in the hands of everyday people who are willing to question, to dream, and to act. So, if you ever find yourself up against a system that feels unfair or impossible to change, remember the quiet bravery of those who came before you. Change starts with a single question. It grows when we talk about it, and it takes root in the choices we make—together. You don’t need all the answers—just the honesty to see things as they are, and the hope to imagine what they could be. Building a fair and free world is never really finished, but every step you take makes a difference. Trust your own common sense. And remember, you’re part of a proud tradition—one where ordinary people choose to shape their own destiny.
